Sale of former Indian Embassy
Building in Bonne
*161. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of  EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to sell 100 years old former Indian Embassy
Building in Bonne, Germany despite strong
objection from the Indian community in
Germany;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether the advertisement for selling
this building appeared in the Daily
Newspaper and the website in Germany; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor?
Miners killed in coal mine accidents
†*162. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) the number of miners killed in
accidents during the last one year in coal
mines operating under subsidiary coal
companies of Coal India Limited in
Jharkhand;
(b) the findings of the Enquiry
Committees constituted for conducting
enquiry into such accidents from time to time;
(c) the number of officials found
responsible for such accidents against
whom action has been taken; and
(d) the steps taken to check such
accidents?
Government representatives in ILO
Conference
†*163. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY: Will the Minister of  LABOUR
AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government sends
representatives of labourers in the I.L.O.
(International Labour Organisation)
Conference;

(b) if so, the criteria adopted to grant
permission to representatives for
participating in the Conference;
(c) whether Government had sent
representatives of labourers in the 93rd
International Labour Conference, recently
held in Geneva;
(d) if so, the aim with which these
representatives had been sent in the above
Conference;
(e) whether it is a fact that Government
had received a proposal from the
International Labour Organisation for
sending the representatives of labourers in

Access to Indians in Pakistani jails
*164. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of  EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the number of Indians held in
Pakistan presently on various charges;
(b) whether Government have any
access to these Indians;
(c) what steps Government propose to
take to ensure that there is regular
communication among these Indian
prisoners and their families in India;
(d) whether any agreement has been
worked out with Pakistan to humanize this
issue; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Safeguarding interests of Indian IT
companies
*165. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will
the Minister of  COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
unscrupulous operators are perpetrating
frauds and duping unsuspecting Indian
companies by giving BPO (Branching
Process Operations) work from Indian or
overseas clients;
(b) if so, whether our existing laws are
adequate to deal with such a situation with
a view to safeguarding interests of Indian
IT companies;
(c) how many such cases were brought
to the notice of Government during 2004
and first six months of 2005;
(d) whether any guidelines have been
issued for the protection of interests of
Indian Companies; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Widening of highways in Tamil Nadu
*166. SHRI R. KAMARAJ: Will the
Minister of  SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
had accorded its approval for converting
the Madurai-Aruppukottai-Tuticorin
Highway into a four lane road;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the other National Highways in
Tamil Nadu that are being converted into
four or six lane for which accord had been
given, recently?
Expansion of communication services
in Orissa
†*167. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR:
Will the Minister of  COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of

51
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
the fact that communication services in
Orissa are in bad condition and their
expansion is taking place at a very slow
pace;
(b) the efforts made by Government to
provide communication services at a fast
speed in the State and what is the outcome
thereof;
(c) by when Orissa is likely to be
brought under cent-per cent communication
services; and
(d) the reasons for not achieving this
target till now?
Level of scientific research in the country
*168. SHRI MANOJ
BHATTACHARYA:
SHRI C.
RAMACHANDRAIAH:
Will the Minister of  SCIENCE AND
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the recent media reports that the Indian
Scientist is a case of pointless and indolent
research;
(b) if so, Government's reaction thereto;
and
(c) the steps proposed to be taken to
rejuvenate the level of scientific research in
the Universities and various scientific
institutes of excellence and make them
professionally useful for developing
technology?
Provision of overloading to washeries
†*169. SHRI RAMADHAR
KASHYAP: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether overloading is provided by
S.E.C.L. in Chhattisgarh to two coal
washeries;
(b) if so, whether these coal washeries
use State highways for transportation;
(c) whether rules under Motor Vehicles
Act are not being violated by providing
such overloading; and
(d) if so, the details in this regard?
MMS clips
*170. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
Minister of  COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that instances of titillating MMS
clips have been on the rise;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the technology in the area
of electronic communication has developed
to such an extent that it is capable of being
misused and abused;
(d) whether there is any legislation to
deal with the abuse of electronic data which
has been doctored;
(e) whether Government propose to
suitably amend the Information Technology
Act of 2000 to deal with the day-to-day
problems of offensive electronic messages;
and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
Demarcation of five points alongwith
the LoC
*171. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of  EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Pakistan has
rejected the proposal on demarcation of
five points alongwith the LoC;
(b) if so, Government's reaction thereto;
and
(c) the reasons for rejecting the proposal
by Pakistan Government?

52
Flat rate for telecom sector
*172. SHRI NILOTPAL BASU: Will
the Minister of  COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are contemplating a flat rate for the whole
country for telecom tariff;
(b) if so, the impact of this on local calls
and long distance calls;
(c) whether it is a fact that the long
distance calls in India are one of the cheapest
in the world;
(d) if not, the comparative rates
elsewhere; and
(e) the possible impact of flat rate on
excessive deficit charges?
Indo-Bangladesh Foreign Secretaries
talks on fencing
*173. SHRI MOOLCHAND
MEENA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of  EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Foreign Secretaries of India
and Bangladesh have agreed to discuss
border fencing;
(b) if so, whether any date has been
fixed for the joint meeting between Foreign
Secretaries on this issue;
(c) whether Bangladesh has stated that
Government have launched a military
crackdown on Indian separatists bases,
prompting security forces on this side of
border to step into high alert to prevent
fleeing militants from entering Indian
territory; and
(d) to what extent border fencing has
been completed uptil now?
Pakistan President's statement
regarding self governance in Kashmir
*174. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of  EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the statement made by
Pakistan President Musharraf to the effect
that solution of Kashmir problem lies not
in autonomy but in ‘self governance’;
(b) whether it is a fact that Hurriyat
Leaders during their recent visit to Pakistan
had also advocated the concept of a United
States of Kashmir from where Kashmiris
can take a plane to Delhi, Islamabad or
Tashkent; and
(c) if so, Government's reaction in regard
thereto and in what manner Government
propose to solve this problem?
Using postman as data collector
*175. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of  COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Indian Postal Department
was established 150  years ago, and at that
time no one would have believed that by
21st century, besides distributing letters,
postmen would knock at your door to
collect consumer data;
(b) if so, whether in that pilot project,
postal department has collected a fairly
comprehensive database of utilization of
Fast Moving Consumable Goods (FMCG)
products, telecom services and using
postmen as data collectors;
(c) if so, by what time this scheme is
likely to be introduced throughout the
country;

53
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(d) to what extent, it has been welcomed
by all; and
(e) to what extent, data has so far been
collected in various parts of the country?
Modernisation of ports
*176. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA
MURTHY: Will the Minister of
SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND
HIGHWAYS be pleased to state the steps
taken so far to expand or modernise various
ports like Karwar, Bhatkal, Honnavar,
Malpe etc.?
Stem cell research
*177. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN:
Will the Minister of  SCIENCE AND
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have examined
the possibility of the country becoming a
nucleus of stem cell research; and
(b) if so, the results thereof?
Attestation of certificates by Ministry
of External Affairs
*178. SHRI THANGA TAMIL
SELVAN: Will the Minister of
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the names of countries which need
the educational certificates to be attested
by the Department of Education and the
Ministry of External Affairs;
(b) whether it is a fact that all the job
aspirants wishing to go to these countries
have to come to Delhi from all over India;
and
(c) whether Government would extend
this facility of attestation to the States as
well?
Implementation of common rates
Under ‘One India’ programme
†*179.SHRIMATI SAVITA SHARDA:
Will the Minister of  COMMUNICA-
TIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have any
proposal to do away with the criteria of
distance to implement the common rates
by removing the Local and STD rates under
‘One India’ programme;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) by when a final decision is likely to
be taken in this regard?
Employment exchanges in Nagaland
*180. SHRI T.R. ZELIANG: Will the
Minister of  LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of jobless persons
registered with employment exchanges in
the State of Nagaland;
(b) the action taken by Government to
provide employment to these persons in
the future; and
(c) whether Government propose to
provide special grants to the States for
youth of NER to give employment
allowance to the unemployed?
